days.note: Climbs the shorter west face of SEWS — 6 pitches of sustained, committing climbing right from the ground with several minor cruxes. The approach to the west side is a bit more direct than the south-face routes; descent follows the standard South Arete downclimb/rappel line.
days.title: Car-to-car climb
days.objective: Climb the Northwest Face (Boving-Pollock) and return to the Blue Lake trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A moderate day: roughly 8.5 hrs car-to-car for 6 pitches on the west-facing wall.

approach_variants.name: Blue Lake Trail to the northwest clearing, then the basin below the west face and the steep corner system
approach_variants.notes:
From the Blue Lake Trailhead, follow the Blue Lake Trail about 1-1.25 miles, roughly an hour, to the clearing and meadow on the spire's northwest side. Leave the trail on the well-worn climber's path and ascend talus and heather into the basin directly below the northwest face.

This is the same basin used to access the southwest rib, Mojo Rising and Free Mojo, so route-finding to the base is shared and only the last few dozen feet along the wall separate the lines.
hazards: Several closely spaced starts on one wall, separated by tens of feet
Committing 5.10 moves on the first pitch before any belay
No documented rappel-the-face option; bailing mid-route means natural gear anchors
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The start is identifiable by a steep corner system, and the first pitch traverses into it. That is the positive test: a steep corner, not a face and not a chimney, entered by traversing rather than climbing straight up. The first pitch makes committing moves at about 5.10 up to a prominent ledge, where some parties belay while others continue to a tree-anchored stance.

The landmark every line on this wall is measured from, and the one to find first: a large chockstone-filled chimney and notch between the two spire formations. Get to that and the wall becomes readable.

Relative to it, the order is countable and in feet: Mojo Rising starts on an obvious bolted face about 20 ft downhill of the chockstone chimney, just left of this route's first pitch. Free Mojo starts roughly 40 ft down and right of the same chimney, on a nondescript crack leading to a two-piece fixed anchor on a pedestal.

So the three-way discriminator is: bolted face 20 ft downhill of the chimney means Mojo Rising. Nondescript crack 40 ft down and right means Free Mojo. Steep corner entered by a traverse means this route. If you are clipping bolts off the ground you are not on the Boving-Pollock.

Six pitches, which makes it the shortest of the west-side lines on this spire, and parties typically continue to the true summit rather than rappel it, then take the standard South Arete descent: downclimb the arete, third and fourth class with a short fifth-class step, to the Rabbit Ears, then three single-rope rappels on a 60 m rope from bolted anchors and chains down the gully to the base.
